passage:
Counsellor's note, Thursday. Jomon, second year, asked to see me after the class group chat blew up over unkind messages about a batchmate, posted by his friend Avni. Several classmates now avoid her. Jomon said he has kept sitting with her at meals, and that it has cost him a few invitations.

He was clear on one point: he would not tell the warden the messages were not hers. "She did it. I told her it was cruel and that she owes an apology." He looked tired, not proud, and twice said he still likes her.

I did not tell him what to do. I asked what he wanted Avni to hear from him. "That I'm not leaving, and that this was wrong."

I have asked Avni to come in tomorrow, and I will check in with the batchmate too.

qa.q: What would Jomon not tell the warden?
qa.a: That the messages were not Avni's.

qa.q: What does Jomon seem to want, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He wants to keep the friendship while staying honest. He keeps sitting with Avni yet says her messages were cruel, and he looks tired rather than proud.

qa.q: What could the counsellor do next to support everyone involved?
qa.a: Meet Avni about making an apology, and check in with the batchmate who was targeted, as the note plans.

qa.q: How might the batchmate see the messages and Jomon's stance?
qa.a: They were probably hurt and left out by the messages, so hearing that someone called them wrong could matter to them.

grounding: Jomon stays loyal to Avni while refusing to cover her harmful behaviour.

passage:
When the tutor flagged Freya's lab report at the University of Melbourne for matching another student's, half their study group turned on her in the group chat within an hour. Chen was the only one who wrote, "Let's not pile on. We don't know everything." Two of them left the chat, and Josh stopped saving him a seat.
That night Freya called. "You'll tell Dr. Okafor we wrote it together, right? That you saw me doing it?"
Chen sat on his bed, the phone warm against his ear. "I'm on your side. I'll keep saying you're more than this. But I'm not lying for you. Did you copy it?"
A long silence. "Some of it. I was drowning."
"Then tell her that. I'll walk to her office with you tomorrow and wait outside."
Freya cried, then agreed. At ten the next morning Chen was on the bench outside Dr. Okafor's door with two coffees.

qa.q: What did Chen write in the group chat?
qa.a: "Let's not pile on. We don't know everything."

qa.q: What was Chen feeling when Freya asked him to lie?
qa.a: Torn: loyal and caring towards Freya, but uneasy about covering for copying, so he asked her for the truth.

qa.q: How did Chen show loyalty without covering for Freya?
qa.a: He defended her from the pile-on, refused to lie to Dr. Okafor, and walked with her to the office and waited outside while she told the truth.

qa.q: How might Freya see Chen's refusal?
qa.a: Hurt at first, then relieved; his steady support made it possible to admit she was drowning and own up.

grounding: Shows standing by a friend at a cost while refusing to cover their wrongdoing, since loyalty includes honesty.

passage:
On the night shift in the women's surgical ward, the senior sister scolded the trainee nurses over a missing chart, and Usha spoke up: "Hemant wasn't on that bed, sister. It wasn't him." It earned her a week of the worst duties.
Two nights later, Hemant caught her by the medicine trolley. "I forgot the 2 a.m. check on bed 14. Just sign that you did it with me. Nobody will know."
Usha's hand stopped on the trolley. She liked Hemant. He had covered her lunch breaks all month.
"I stood up for you because you were right," she whispered. "This is different. If bed 14 needed something and we hide it, someone could get hurt."
"You'll get me into trouble."
"Let's check on her now, together. Then you tell sister. I'll stand next to you."
They went. The patient was fine, asleep. Hemant told the senior sister before handover, his voice low. Usha stood beside him, as promised.

qa.q: What made Usha hesitate at the medicine trolley?
qa.a: She felt torn: fond of and grateful to Hemant, who had covered her lunch breaks, but worried that a patient could get hurt if they hid the missed check.

qa.q: What did Usha do to be both loyal and honest?
qa.a: She refused to sign, went with Hemant to check the patient straight away, and stood beside him while he told the senior sister.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Usha's refusal?
qa.a: As risky and unfair at first ("You'll get me into trouble"), though her standing beside him shows she is still on his side.

grounding: Illustrates loyalty to a colleague that includes honesty, defending him against unfair blame but not covering a missed patient check.
